newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-STEINBRENNER THROWN OFF EXECUTIVE COUNCIL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-STEINBRENNER THROWN OFF EXECUTIVE COUNCIL.

text.p: Major League Baseball decided to punish George Steinbrenner on Tuesday for cutting his own marketing deal and for suing fellow owners by suspending the New York Yankees owner from his position on baseball's ruling Executive Council.

Baseball brass, already upset by Steinbrenner's 10-year, $95 million marketing deal with the adidas sports apparel company, were outraged when the contentious Yankees boss filed a lawsuit last week, claiming that his fellow owners conspired to prevent him from implementing the deal.

The Executive Council made the decision during a meeting to which Steinbrenner was not invited. The 10-member Executive Council has been ruling over Major League Baseball since the owners forced out the sport's last real commissioner, Fay Vincent.
Steinbrenner also was suspended from his positions on all other baseball committees and the council ruled that no other Yankees executive may take his place.
The sanctions however are far less drastic than Steinbrenner's two previous suspensions from baseball and he will be able to continue running the team.
The Yankees and adidas announced their deal in March, bringing immediate protest from fellow owners on the grounds that it undermined baseball's ability to sign marketing deals on a national basis.

Steinbrenner and adidas filed the lawsuit last Tuesday in U.S. District Court in Tampa, Florida, challenging baseball's precious anti-trust exemption. As part of the Major League Agreement, however, teams and their owners are prohibited from suing the commissioner's office, which is the basis for Tuesday's sanctions.
The Executive Council had ordered the Yankees to stop selling T-shirts with adidas logos and to stop the Yankees ground crew from wearing adidas logos on their work uniforms.

Baseball's Agency Agreement stipulates that baseball and its properties division are the exclusive brokers for all marketing deals involving uniforms, caps and such merchandise, and that the clubs would share equally in the proceeds.

Russell Athletic Corp. currently owns the rights to manufacture all major-league uniforms. But the value of that deal would be diminished without the World Series champion Yankees, one of the most recognisable teams in sports.

Steinbrenner has twice been suspended from baseball, first in 1974 for making illegal campaign contributions to President Richard Nixon, and again in 1990 for financial dealings with a known gambler. Both those suspensions, handed down by actual commissioners, banned Steinbrenner from the game and kept him from running the club.
